title: Distributed execution: partitions, shuffle and memory usage

videos.script: A job is cut into stages, and every cut is a shuffle. {{stages}} Inside a stage, steps chain together, one pass over the data. Between stages, every row is written to local disk by one set of tasks and fetched by another. {{shuffle}} This lesson measures that. Two groupings that read the same twenty-four million rows. One shuffles almost nothing. The other shuffles thirty-five megabytes, because the key has a million values. {{measure}} Then memory. An executor of seven hundred and sixty-eight megabytes gives Spark two hundred and eighty of them. You will watch a sort spill most of its data to disk, and finish first anyway. {{memory}} And the one place that never spills: the driver. Bring everything back with collect, and it stops. {{driver}}
